correspondence.component_scope: southwestern opening and northward plain
correspondence.finding: The opening occupies wooded and partly cleared inland plain, continuing north and then east through the same broad dry-land setting. The imagery establishes the local terrain corridor, without identifying a spring, channel head, named river or present flow. These dry stretches are not rejected merely because a wet channel is absent.

correspondence.component_scope: western shallow depressions and cultivated approach
correspondence.finding: The selection continues northeast through cultivated and wooded ground into shallow pale and dark depression patches south of the western settlement. Broad local receiving-floor correspondence is visible; small lateral hollows and field boundaries are not promoted to named tributaries or active canals.

correspondence.component_scope: long upper middle cultivated transfer
correspondence.finding: The long eastward part crosses the cultivated plain among separated shallow depressions. Ground coverage is complete, but the inspected material does not establish the receiving connection from the western depression floor to the eastern lagoon belt across this substantial interval. The issue is the inter-depression transfer, not exact alignment with field drains or absence of present water.

correspondence.component_scope: middle lagoon margin and southgoing depression
correspondence.finding: The eastward approach reaches a pale lagoon/depression margin and then turns southeast and south through a recognizable elongated lowland belt. Its dry floor, cultivated interruptions and small model shortcuts are accepted at ordinary geographic scale. No exact shore, water level or lagoon hydronym is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: southern cross belt transfer
correspondence.finding: The selection leaves the first elongated depression belt, turns east across cultivated tracts and small depression patches, then bends northeast toward a separate eastern lagoon complex. The local floors on both sides are visible. The ordinary receiving connection between these distinct depression belts remains unestablished by the inspected sources; neither seasonal wetness nor a continuously surveyed bank is required.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern lagoon complex and northeast return
correspondence.finding: The selected northeastward return lies across the broad pale/dark lagoon complex and its adjoining cultivated depression floor, including the transport-corridor surroundings. Local terrain and receiving-setting correspondence is visible. A precise culvert, road-crossing hydraulic route or present management operation is not inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: actual cultivated endpoint
correspondence.finding: The final part ends in a cultivated tract within the eastern shallow-depression plain. The actual endpoint is retained there, without substituting a nearby visible lagoon or inventing a river mouth. The final local terrain setting is observed independently of the unresolved upstream cross-belt transfers.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and northward Modoc Creek valley
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is on the Modoc Creek valley north of the Paul Reservoir side branch. It proceeds north through the mapped enclosed stream corridor, then bends northeast into the broader marshy lower Modoc setting. Paul Reservoir is separately mapped southeast of the opening and is not a selected lake passage. East Fork Big Beaver Creek lies in a different adjacent western valley. The chosen opening is not asserted to be the official source of Modoc Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern marshy Modoc passage and Beaver Creek join
correspondence.finding: The selected northeast/east arc stays in the continuous mapped lower Modoc marsh-and-stream receiving floor and reaches Beaver Creek near the I-15/Boatman Springs crossing. A directly mapped channel, shared low marsh floor and downstream Beaver corridor establish ordinary connectivity; no exact active thread across each wetland step is asserted. The separate upstream Beaver/Big Beaver and Long Creek approaches are not renamed Modoc.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Beaver Creek valley south from Humphrey
correspondence.finding: The selection turns south in the repeatedly labeled Beaver Creek valley, passing Humphrey and the Pleasant Valley vicinity. Tributaries such as Idaho Creek, Pleasant Valley Creek, Miners Creek, Stoddard Creek and Dry Creek remain separate side drainages. The selected line remains in the receiving Beaver valley at ordinary cartographic scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Mountain exit, Troutline junction and southwestward bend
correspondence.finding: The route follows Beaver Creek past its mountain-front exit and the distinct Troutline/Rattlesnake eastern tributary setting. It then bends southwest across I-15 and turns south in the mapped Beaver valley; the western Dry Creek approach is a tributary rather than a replacement name for the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Beaver Creek through Dubois and the lower plain
correspondence.finding: The selected long southward interval corresponds to the repeatedly labeled Beaver Creek channel through Dubois and across the lower plain. South of the town the map shows several intermittent threads and an expanded western receiving corridor; the selected westward bow and return remain in that connected Beaver setting. The parallel highway and railroad are not treated as waterways.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Beaver Creek and Camas Creek receiving junction
correspondence.finding: The selection continues south from the expanded Beaver corridor toward Camas, where the separately mapped eastern Camas Creek joins the same receiving network. It then turns southwest under the Camas Creek name. The generalized selected bend is assessed within the common mapped junction setting, without forcing it to a surveyed confluence vertex or particular parallel thread. IDFG independently describes Beaver Creek as a Camas tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Camas Creek through refuge wetlands and pond/lake setting
correspondence.finding: Below the junction the route follows the southwest Camas Creek corridor and turns south through the western Camas National Wildlife Refuge wetlands. Directly mapped channels, broad marshes and the connected Rays Lake-side receiving setting support the passage. Two-way Pond, Willow Pond, Rat Farm Pond, Sandhole Lake, Leavitz Pond and Warm Creek are distinct named neighboring features; their names do not become aliases of the selected river. The route is not assigned to an exact presently managed water-control path.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Camas Creek and eastern Mud Lake approach
correspondence.finding: The route leaves the southern refuge lake/wetland setting and turns southwest then west in the repeatedly labeled Camas Creek corridor through agricultural land. The ordinary stream/modified-channel corridor continues to the eastern Mud Lake margin. Nearby ditches, roads and the Owsley Canal at the lake are distinct features, not names for the full selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Source terminal retained separately
correspondence.finding: The source endpoint lies inside the mapped Mud Lake waterbody after the final westward lake-interior extension. The terminal is a receiving lake/sink setting, not an additional named river reach or a claim about current lake depth. IDFG describes the earlier seasonal Camas sink and later diking; this supplies historical context only.

correspondence.component_scope: Rendered terminal retained separately
correspondence.finding: The rendered endpoint is stored separately and coincides with the source endpoint inside Mud Lake. Both are assessed in the same mapped lake-interior receiving setting. The line is not extended to an outlet, moved to a bank or equated with Owsley Canal.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern dry-valley opening and westward feeder into Arroyo Seco
correspondence.finding: The selected opening occupies a shallow dry valley on the mesa, runs south, turns southwest and follows the westward low floor into the named receiving arroyo. Clear photographic landforms and surrounding topographic relief support the entire ordinary receiving connection. No separate basin transfer is required. The feeder remains unnamed; nearby road, ranch and draw labels are not transferred to it.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward upper Arroyo Seco and its southwest canyon reach
correspondence.finding: Direct labels follow the receiving intermittent drainage south and southwest through its incised corridor. The selected route stays in that corridor to the Chupadera joining area. Alamillo Arroyo is a separate entering branch; its name is not an alias or a separate selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Arroyo Seco to Chupadera Arroyo junction and immediate downstream continuation
correspondence.finding: The source depicts Arroyo Seco entering Chupadera Arroyo from the northeast, followed by the selected southwest continuation on the receiving trunk. The separately labeled Chupadera upper branch arrives from the north and is not the selected opening. This is a mapped joining relationship, not a nearest-name assignment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest Chupadera Arroyo trunk and adjoining alluvial corridor
correspondence.finding: Repeated direct Chupadera Arroyo labels lie on the selected receiving valley. Surrounding tributary fans enter the same corridor, including the separate Rancho Viejo Arroyo setting. Generalized selected bends remain within the connected valley and do not establish a uniform name for every upstream branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Broad middle valley, lower trunk and U.S. 380 crossing
correspondence.finding: The selection continues down the same axial valley through locally incised and wider dry-floor reaches, receives smaller eastern and western drainages, and crosses U.S. 380. Intermittent linework appears at different display scales, while relief and valley continuity remain coherent. No lake, glacier or managed-reservoir transfer is required along this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward lower dry wash and broad northern Jornada del Muerto floor
correspondence.finding: The lower arroyo passes into a broad continuous low-relief receiving floor west of the Oscura Mountains. Clear topographic contours and the photographic corridor establish the ordinary southward continuation despite diffuse drainage and some cloud-obscured image patches. The independent field-study prose identifies this drainage as Chupadera Draw, mapped as Chupadera Arroyo, and describes its playa receiving setting. No currently wet thread is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southern dry-floor passage and coincident source/render ending
correspondence.finding: The final selected parts stay on the same broad basin floor. Stored source and rendered endings coincide within this receiving setting; neither is extended to the Rio Grande or the sea. No present named lake or distinct perennial terminal channel is identified at the endpoint. The paleo-Lake Trinity description is regional historical context, not a current-waterbody naming assignment.

correspondence.component_scope: selected southeastern opening and southward wash
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening follows a dissected interior-hill wash, initially eastward and then southward. Side gullies merge into a broader pale arroyo floor. The photographic view distinguishes the selected opening and southern approach from neighboring gullies; no upstream hydronym is supplied.

correspondence.component_scope: southern receiving flat and westward turn
correspondence.finding: The southward wash opens into a broad dry receiving flat at the southern bend. The selected route turns west and northwest across this continuous alluvial floor, with foothills bounding the southern margin. Ordinary receiving-floor correspondence is established without requiring a visible wet thread through the flat.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestern bend and intermontane wash
correspondence.finding: The western side of the southern flat leads into the north-northwestward intermontane arroyo. Visible side-gully joins and the same low corridor account for the western turn and its continuation along the mountain foot. The generalized municipal drainage is compatible with this broad setting; no named separate-basin transfer is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: middle wash to el llano receiving floor
correspondence.finding: The intermontane wash continues north to a broad central alluvial/playa floor and bends northwest across it. The Camargo map places El Llano on this receiving depression and Laguna Los Tanques beside the southeastern approach. The aerial view shows the selected approach, broad floor and northward continuation as one ordinary geographic lowland passage; it does not establish current water exchange between named waterbodies.

correspondence.component_scope: elongated northern lowland and eastern joins
correspondence.finding: The route continues north along a long, narrow pale flat between western relief and eastern fan surfaces. Several larger eastern washes join this lowland; the Las Arenosas setting is a separate eastern branch on the municipal map. The continuous dry floor is sufficient for ordinary correspondence across the nearly straight stored middle parts.

correspondence.component_scope: northern wash and alluvial apron
correspondence.finding: Beyond the central lowland, the selected corridor bends northwest through a visible dry wash and widening alluvial apron. East- and west-side tributary washes enter the same floor. The photographic source supplies the geographic coverage north of the Camargo map footprint rather than extending that municipal map beyond its published area.

correspondence.component_scope: terminal approach and closed playa
correspondence.finding: The northern arroyo and fan floor continue northwest into a distinct light-colored closed playa. The final stored part reaches the playa interior, not merely the upstream inlet. Its mapped source endpoint and rendered endpoint coincide in this receiving setting and are separately retained below. No river or terminal-playa name is assigned from unlabelled imagery.
